title: Barnaby at eight, i
logline: Monday. The dog is eight. The strip notices the middle of a life by drawing the walk at its exact usual pace for the first time — not slow yet, not fast anymore. The pace of a dog who knows the route.

panels.composition: The beach road. BARNABY, eight, trotting ahead at a pace that is neither of the paces the strip has drawn. WOOD behind.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a middle-aged dog trotting at an easy knowing pace down a road toward a beach with a thin man walking behind, no words

panels.composition: The dog stopping at the exact post he always stops at. Not sniffing. Checking.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a dog pausing at a wooden post to check it rather than sniff it, no words

panels.composition: The stairs. The dog going down without looking back — he knows Wood's there.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a dog going down bluff stairs without looking back while a man follows, no words

panels.composition: The beach. The dog at the log, already lying down, before Wood reaches the sand. The route, known.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a dog already lying down at a drift log while a thin man is still reaching the bottom of the stairs, no words

art.palette: limited; Sundays in watercolor, good now
art.paper: bristol; the browser; from 2008 coastal newsprint a week behind

notes: Wordless. The middle pace. The route, known.
